analysis.title: 'Market Feels Healthy & Unhealthy At Same Time': Goldman Partner Says Traditional Correlations Are 'A Bit Broken'
key_insights: Molavi says the market feels healthy and unhealthy at once. Headline equity levels are at odds with sentiment and volatility beneath the surface. Traditional correlations are broken for now: equities vs yields, index vol vs single-stock/theme/factor vol, equity levels vs gross, var vs gross, rates vol vs equity vol.

Macro stress signals are all flashing: Middle East re-escalation or no solution, sticky high oil, record diesel prices and shortages, yields rallying or at all-time highs, IPOs pulled, rate hikes and central bank policy shifts, inflation above target. Equities are at all-time highs regardless.

The week's rally was sustained by a dovish trifecta of soft jobs, tame PCE and the G7 oil release. That shifted odds toward a Fed pause and eventual easing and eased diesel and inflation pressure. Molavi describes a weekly round trip back to the starting point, with a different reason holding the market up each week rather than anything structural.

Beneath record index levels: homebuilders down 15-20% in the last month, violent semis vs software seesaws, whipsaw in real assets and high-ROIC vs duration, harder-to-manage shorts and crowding, consumer inertia coming under AI disruption pressure, euro banks hit by euro sovereign concerns, and K-shaped consumer dispersion.

Mega-cap leadership continues: Meta has risen sharply in recent weeks, Nvidia hit an all-time high Friday and is approaching $6 trillion market cap, Microsoft is up 50% from its July lows and positive on the year. Micro and index look healthy but are narrow and dependent on one theme.

Equities are less linked to macro than expected. As long as belief in AI and AI capex holds, oil, rate policy, deficit, jobs, yields, geopolitics and politics are secondary in the market's weighing. Molavi calls narrowness and concentration a feature of this market rather than a bug, which could change.

Three pillars to watch: yields/rates, oil and the AI theme. Secondary questions are central bank policy and when high yields become too high and break things, oil pressure relief (reserve release) vs solutions (ceasefires), and the end game for AI. October is heavy with Treasury auctions, earnings, elections, geopolitics and politics.

Flows are producing repeated outsized moves in JGBs, OATs, global front-end rates, Mag7 ETFs, gold, and Hynix and Korea earlier this year. Retail and institutional flows are increasingly correlated, adding velocity. Moves are increasingly binary: all selling with no buyers or all buying with no supply.

Political stress is building: social unrest in Spain, French budget negotiations, UK budget and Labour manifesto, Bolsonaro vs Lula in Brazil, and US midterms. Molavi sees politics shifting toward the wings, with more shouting, less governing and a risk of violent policy shifts. Data centres and AI are being politicised in the US.

Geopolitics: troop increases in Iran, return of terrorism, Russia/Ukraine continuing, and a US/Xi summit with US/China as the 'big game'. Molavi frames a new economic Cold War with tariffs and technology linked, second-order allegiances (China buying energy from Russia/Iran), chip-sale rules, and subsidy and price wars in solar, EV and green tech (Tesla vs 150 Chinese EV makers). He expects a more fragmented trading world.

Yields: US 10-year and 30-year are rising despite a Fed hike. The 30-year is around 6.25%, the highest since 2002. UK 30-year is around 6.25%, the highest since 1998. France just had its worst quarter since the euro was created over 25 years ago. Causes vary by country: hot economy, fiscal spiral, deficits, inflation, central bank policy, competing supply (AI capex issuance) and a shift in buyers.

France: the CAC is one of the only global markets down on the year. The OAT market is under heavy stress with de-risking flows. Knock-on effects include costlier domestic lending, slower credit to households and firms, and a worse fiscal deficit. The ECB is constrained financially, politically and legally. ECB government debt holdings are up EUR 1.4 trillion since Lagarde said the ECB is not there to close spreads. France may fall outside the TPI backstop given spring 2027 elections.

Southern Europe is attracting foreign investment (Solaria and PPC deals with hyperscalers), talent and political and fiscal stability, with Meloni the longest-serving leader in Europe. Caution: higher yields hurt real estate, house prices in Greece, Spain and Portugal are up materially, and real GDP there has the highest correlation to real estate in Europe.

AI capex historical analogy: railways 1845, utilities 1929, Japan 1989, dot-com 2000, shale 2014. Molavi says the trigger is normally a central bank pivot, and the order is stocks peak, capex keeps rising for 6 to 24 months, then capex rolls, then stocks roll.

Concentration in one trade as % of S&P market cap: railroads 1830s 63%, utilities 1920s 36%, Nifty Fifty 1972 40%, Japan 1985 44%, TMT 1999 41%, AI big 10 now 42%, which could rise with one or two new IPOs.

Issuance shows signs of trouble: poor performance of secondary sell-downs globally and paused US IPOs. The market is more discerning than in H1's 'bring it and I'll buy it'. Bulls call it price discipline. Bears point to slowing retail momentum and a public-private bid-offer gap.

Mixed signals: S&P and Nasdaq are at all-time highs while the job market is at a 10-year low on Molavi's blend of hiring, quits, openings, hours, wages, temp jobs, claims, Sahm rule and postings. He says the market is no longer a proxy for the economy but a narrow representation of about 10 of the top 50 stocks focused on AI.

Speed of value creation: Anthropic went from zero to about $2 trillion in 5 years, and Lovable and Cursor reached $500m+ ARR in around a year. In venture, Sequoia invested in Ineffable Intelligence at a $55m valuation and about a month later Index and Lightspeed invested at $4bn and $5.1bn in the same round. Thinking Machines Lab raised at $12bn pre-product.
Bottleneck: data centre deployment likely caps out at 20-25 GW by early next year because of delays, politics and supply bottlenecks. Only 72% of pre-AI data centre builds came online on time.

Closing analogy: annual photographs rose from a few thousand in 1840 to 2 trillion this year, 94% on smartphones, despite casualties such as Polaroid. Molavi's point is that the only constant is change.

ZeroHedge's summary: Molavi's claim is that the stress list has been demoted rather than being wrong. None of oil, multi-decade-high yields, an unresolved Middle East, a weak labor market or French bonds is setting the price while belief in AI capex holds. October's auctions, earnings, elections and geopolitics test that.

tension_points.theme: equity record highs vs macro stress
tension_points.bull_case: Dovish trifecta of soft jobs, tame PCE and the G7 oil release shifted odds toward a Fed pause and eventual easing, supporting long-duration growth, real assets and hard money. AI capex belief keeps mega-cap leadership intact.
tension_points.bear_case: Oil, yields, diesel shortages, inflation, a 10-year-low labor market and French bond stress are all unresolved. The index is a narrow bet on one theme, and a weekly round trip shows the rally rests on one-off narratives.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Belief in AI and AI capex breaking, or a central bank pivot, which Molavi says historically precedes stocks peaking, then capex rolling, then stocks rolling.

tension_points.bull_case: Pause and weak secondary sell-downs reflect healthy price discipline.
tension_points.bear_case: Slowing retail momentum and FOMO, plus a public-private bid-offer gap too wide to cross, point to a liquidity problem.

theme_stances.theme: AI concentration and capex cycle risk
theme_stances.key_argument: Concentration near historical peaks and the sequence of stocks peaking, capex rising, then both rolling after a central bank pivot is the template Molavi hopes will not repeat.
theme_stances.evidence: stocks peak, capex keeps rising (for 6 to 24 months), then capex roll

theme_stances.key_argument: Equities are decoupled from macro as long as belief in AI capex holds, and traditional correlations are broken for now.
theme_stances.evidence: traditional correlations are, for now, a bit broken

theme_stances.key_argument: French OAT stress is spreading to lending and the fiscal deficit, and the ECB is politically and legally constrained and may not use the TPI backstop for France.
